question: Who will win the 2026 Tennessee Democratic gubernatorial primary?

factors.description: Prediction markets priced Green ~94% to win the nomination (stale April 2026 data, thin volume)
Green is the only elected official, has ~13x fundraising lead ($703K), and leads the only poll (14% vs McCants 11%); from Memphis, TN's largest Democratic base
62% undecided in a low-information crowded field; TN Dem primary electorate is heavily Black, and low-info races can break on demographic/name factors favoring McCants (pastor) or Atwater
McCants polled 11%, close second, only 3pp behind Green (within MOE)

summary: Jerri Green is the dominant frontrunner in the August 6, 2026 Tennessee Democratic gubernatorial primary — the only elected official in the field, with a ~13x fundraising lead ($703K), a lead in the only public poll (Green 14%, McCants 11%), and prediction market pricing near 94%. I discount the market to ~80% to reflect the 62% undecided share in a low-information, crowded field where Tennessee's disproportionately Black Democratic primary electorate could break toward McCants or Atwater in ways not captured by fundraising. McCants (close poll second) and Atwater (prior statewide/mayoral candidate) absorb most of the residual probability; Cyr, Kurtz, and write-ins are negligible.

**Reasoning:** Green is the clear frontrunner — the only elected official in the field, with a dominant fundraising lead (~$703K, ~13x her nearest rival), a lead in the only public poll (14% vs McCants 11%), and prediction markets near 94%. I discounted below the market to 80% because the 62% undecided share in this low-information primary creates genuine uncertainty: Tennessee's heavily-Black Democratic primary electorate could plausibly break toward McCants (a pastor polling a close second) or Atwater in ways that fundraising and endorsements don't capture.
